value: Powers of 2 (positions right-to-left carry weights 2^0=1, 2^1=2, 2^2=4, 2^3=8 decimal)
note: Definition of a base-2 positional system. Powers of 10 is decimal; 3 and 5 are unrelated bases.
Bits of 1010 right-to-left: b0=0, b1=1, b2=0, b3=1. Leftmost 1 is b3, weight 2^3=8. D (2^4=16) would require a 5-bit number; 1010 has only 4 positions (b0..b3).

value: Nibble = 4 bits (a nibble spans decimal values 0-15)
note: Byte=8 bits, kilobyte=1024 bytes, word is machine-dependent (typically 16/32/64 bits).

value: LSB = the rightmost bit of 11001, which is a 1 with weight 2^0 = 1 decimal. Whole number 11001 binary = 25 decimal
note: Bits right-to-left: b0=1, b1=0, b2=0, b3=1, b4=1. The least significant position b0 happens to hold a 1, so 'the rightmost 1' identifies it correctly and unambiguously.

value: MSB = the leftmost bit of 11001, a 1 with weight 2^4 = 16 decimal. Whole number 11001 binary = 16+8+0+0+1 = 25 decimal
note: b4=1 is the highest-weight position. Option B ('second 1 from the right') points at b3, weight 2^3=8 decimal, which is not the MSB. Only one option is true.

value: 10102 is NOT valid binary - it contains the digit 2, which does not exist in base 2. (Read as a decimal numeral it is 10102 decimal; as an intended binary string it is malformed.)
note: A=001011 is valid (leading zeros permitted) = 11 decimal; B=1100 valid = 12 decimal; D=0 valid = 0 decimal. Only C uses an out-of-range digit.

value: A power of 2. A single 1 at position k equals 2^k: 1, 10, 100, 1000 binary = 1, 2, 4, 8 decimal
note: Checked each distractor against the set {1,2,4,8,16,...}: 2 is prime but not greater than 2 and no larger power of 2 is prime, so A fails; 1 is not composite and every other member is even, so B fails; none is divisible by 3, so D fails. Exactly one true option.
Fractional positions mirror the integer side with negative exponents of the base. C is the decimal-point weighting; A and D are non-negative exponents.
